comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Root cause CONFIRMED empirically at ALL THREE sites, through the real emit() path.

Two-clone harness (bare remote + clones A/B sharing one tickets branch, base padded to the retention bound, both clones taken offline, one automatic emit each):
- pre-prune CONTROL merge: rc=0 every run
- plan_review/sidecar.py:89  -> CONFLICT (rename/rename)
- code_review/sidecar.py:147 -> CONFLICT (rename/rename)
- completion_sidecar.py:59   -> CONFLICT (rename/rename)
Conflict text shows the shared base file 'renamed to' a DIFFERENT new UUID in each clone - the delete(oldest)+add(new-uuid) pairing that git rename detection resolves as a rename conflict.

Contract violated: docs/concurrency.md invariant I1 - convergence is 'never by deleting a committed event (I1 append-only)'. Prior art: bug 8185 / commit be8a0c059 removed the same mechanism from enrich_drain and overlap/digest_sidecar and explicitly spawned this ticket for the three siblings.

IMPORTANT nuance for anyone re-testing: rename detection is content-similarity based and rebar events are single-line minified JSON, so a one-byte length difference between the pruned and the new event can drop similarity below git's 50%% threshold and the merge spuriously succeeds. Build the base from a REAL emitted payload (equal-length neighbour) or the repro looks green. This is why the wedge appears intermittent in production and is then permanent.

FIX: removed the automatic prune() call from all three emit() paths (net -3 executable lines + docs). prune() itself is KEPT, importable and behaviourally unchanged, as an EXPLICIT operator-invoked operation - existing direct-call tests still pass untouched. Growth bound is a deliberately deferred tradeoff; merge-safe bounded retention is tracked as 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d.

Two pre-existing tests in tests/unit/test_audit_retention_cap.py asserted the DEFECT (test_code_review_emit_calls_prune: 'emit must prune the target ticket after appending'; test_code_review_emit_retains_the_cap: emit->prune wiring caps at 50). Both were added by story fde0, which introduced the automatic code-review prune this bug removes. They were INVERTED in place (not deleted) to pin the append-only invariant where the defect used to be, following the fix-out -> revise -> verify RED -> fix-in ordering.

SIBLING SWEEP (clean): every remaining delete_events call now sits inside an explicit operator-invoked prune(); zero automatic invocations remain in src/rebar. purge_bridge.py is the operator 'rebar purge-bridge' command.

NOTE on the AWS lead: the available AWS account holds an unrelated project (no instances in 17 regions, review-bot host not reachable), so NO production corroboration was obtained. The conclusion rests on the local two-clone experiment plus 8185's closed-bug record.

comments.body:
HANDOFF TO EPIC 061c (owns the two sidecar files) — RCA CONFIRMED, EXACT FIX DOCUMENTED, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.

WHY THIS IS BEING REPARENTED, NOT LANDED BY THIS SESSION: the fix must edit src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py and src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py, both on epic 061c's protected file list. 061c has a large in-flight Gerrit stack; editing these from a separate change would collide. Reparenting under 061c so that session lands it within its own stack without disruption. The third site (code_review/sidecar.py) is NOT 061c's but is kept together here so the fix stays one coherent unit (identical mechanism at all three sites).

STATUS ON CURRENT main (tip 253224f354): the dead session 2b0c5f01 documented a fix in an earlier comment but it NEVER landed — verified all three emit() paths still auto-call prune() on origin/main. So this is still a live defect.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed empirically by the prior session's two-clone harness; mechanism re-verified against current main): each sidecar emit() appends a new UUID-named event and then automatically calls prune(), which uses _store.event_append.delete_events to physically delete older committed UUID event files. Across two independent tracker clones that share the tickets branch, delete(oldest)+add(new-uuid) in each clone makes git's rename detection resolve the shared base file as 'renamed to' a DIFFERENT new UUID in each clone -> rename/rename CONFLICT on union merge, wedging reconvergence. This violates docs/concurrency.md I1 (append-only): 'convergence ... never by deleting a committed event (I1 append-only)' (docs/concurrency.md:168). Prior art: bug 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282 / commit be8a0c059 removed the identical mechanism from enrich_drain + overlap/digest_sidecar and explicitly spawned THIS ticket for the three siblings. NUANCE: git rename detection is content-similarity based and rebar events are single-line minified JSON, so a one-byte length difference between the pruned and new event can drop similarity below git's 50% threshold and the merge spuriously succeeds — build the two-clone base from a REAL emitted payload (equal-length neighbour) or the repro looks green. This is why the wedge is intermittent in production and then permanent.

EXACT FIX (net -3 executable lines in src/, prune() kept as operator-invoked):
  1. src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py — DELETE line 89: 'prune(verdict.get("ticket_id", ""), repo_root=repo_root)  # best-effort retention'. Keep line 90 'return True'.
  2. src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py — DELETE line 148: 'prune(target_ticket, repo_root=repo_root)  # best-effort retention (bounds code-review growth)'. Keep line 149 'return True'.
  3. src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py — DELETE line 59: 'prune(str(verdict.get("ticket_id") or ""), repo_root=repo_root)  # best-effort retention'. Keep line 60 'return True'.
  In all three, prune() itself (the def and its delete_events call) is UNCHANGED and remains importable as an EXPLICIT operator-invoked op — only the AUTOMATIC call from emit() is removed. The prune() return value is unused at the call site, so removal is clean.

TEST CHANGES:
  - tests/unit/test_audit_retention_cap.py: two tests currently assert the DEFECT and must be INVERTED in place (not deleted), following fix-out -> revise -> verify RED -> fix-in: test_code_review_emit_calls_prune (line 95; 'emit must prune the target ticket after appending', line 101) and test_code_review_emit_retains_the_cap (line 80; asserts emit->prune caps at 50). Re-point them to pin the append-only invariant (emit() appends and does NOT delete any committed event) where the defect used to be. These tests were added by story fde0, which introduced the automatic code-review prune this bug removes; direct-call prune() tests stay untouched and green.
  - Add real two-clone RED reproductions (bare remote + clones A/B sharing one tickets branch, base padded to the retention bound from a real emitted payload, both clones offline, one automatic emit each) for each of the three emit paths: pre-fix -> rename/rename CONFLICT; post-fix -> clean union reconverge (rc=0). Run under the full concurrency tier + mutation check (re-add the prune() call -> back to RED).

FILE IMPACT: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py, src/rebar/llm/code_review/sidecar.py, src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py, tests/unit/test_audit_retention_cap.py, plus new two-clone repro test(s). ACs unchanged (see description).

DEFERRED TRADEOFF: removing automatic prune means sidecar event files grow unbounded per ticket. Merge-safe bounded retention is deliberately deferred and tracked separately as 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d. SIBLING SWEEP was clean: after this fix, every remaining delete_events call sits inside an explicit operator-invoked prune() (e.g. purge_bridge.py behind 'rebar purge-bridge') — zero automatic invocations remain in src/rebar.

DEFECT LEGITIMACY: defect (violates cited I1 append-only invariant + prior closed bug 8185 for the identical mechanism). Caller/dependency gate: prune() retained for operators; only the automatic emit-time call is removed, so no caller depending on emit's return (a bool) is affected.

compiled_state.description:
## Context
Plan-review, code-review, and completion sidecar emit paths automatically prune older committed UUID-named event files through delete_events. This repeats the destructive-retention mechanism proven to wedge the review-bot tracker in bug 8185-2d4b-d2bf-4282.

## Evidence
- The two-clone experiment for 8185 proved that deleting a shared base sidecar while each stale clone appends a replacement makes Git infer rename conflicts.
- plan_review/sidecar.py, code_review/sidecar.py, and completion_sidecar.py each call delete_events from automatic retention.
- The store concurrency contract requires independent UUID events to reconverge by append-only union.

## Plan
- Build real two-clone RED reproductions for each automatic emit/retention path.
- Remove or replace automatic physical deletion only where the runtime experiment proves conflict.
- Preserve latest-result readers, audit history, reducer behavior, and clean tracker state.
- Verify each path RED to GREEN with mutation checks and the full concurrency tier.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Real two-clone tests prove each affected automatic sidecar path reconverges cleanly.
- [ ] Automatic sidecar writes do not physically delete committed UUID event files.
- [ ] Latest-result readers still select the newest valid sidecar.
- [ ] Focused, default, integration, lint, and typecheck gates pass.
compiled_state.title: Automatic LLM sidecar retention can diverge independent tracker clones
